The AgentTuning paper names AgentInstruct as its 1,866-trajectory dataset and points to the authors' AgentTuning repository; the official organization dataset card cites the same paper and trajectory count.
The ToolLLM paper introduces ToolBench and identifies the OpenBMB/ToolBench repository as the released project. No official Hugging Face dataset page was established.

The CVPR 2009 paper and ImageNet-operated site describe the same WordNet-organized image database. This generic family link does not assert that every bare ImageNet mention specifies the ILSVRC-2012 1K subset.
The PLOS ONE paper introduces the Socio-Moral Image Database (SMID) and explicitly identifies the OSF project as the location of its images and normative data.
The authors' LlavaGuard project and repository link the AIML-TUDA Hugging Face release as the annotated dataset associated with arXiv:2406.05113.

The MM-SafetyBench paper introduces the benchmark and gives isXinLiu/MM-SafetyBench as its resource repository. The previously cited BlueSuffix repository is downstream use, not MM-SafetyBench's official repository.
The ACL paper defines the crafted D_det and D_ext training datasets and identifies the authors' indirect-pia-detection repository; its data directory contains the released assets.
The X-Teaming paper explicitly publishes the marslabucla/XGuard-Train dataset URL, and the authors' x-teaming repository/project links the same release.
The ActorAttack paper introduces SafeMTData and names the ActorAttack repository; the SafeMTData organization dataset card cites arXiv:2410.10700 and uses the exact dataset name.
The audited citation refers generically to Wikipedia dump files from Wikimedia Downloads; dumps.wikimedia.org is Wikimedia's first-party dump index, not a similarly named derived dataset.
The exact cited title, author, year, and 3,824-article description resolve through DOI 10.7910/DVN/GMFCTR to the Harvard Dataverse dataset, establishing identity beyond the generic name.
The authors' LaMini-LM project page links both the repository and MBZUAI/LaMini-instruction, describes the 2.58M instruction-response pairs, and cites arXiv:2304.14402.

The benchmark paper names BIPIA and the Microsoft repository identifies itself as the data and code release for that same paper. The repository does not establish a completed official Hugging Face release.
